 Stephen Curry, Brandin Podziemski, Yaxel Lendeborg, Draymond Green and Graham Ike will start Friday’s game against the Grizzlies. 
 Podziemski is available after missing Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers due to a lower-back injury. His return means that De’Anthony Melton will come off the bench. Ike gets his first NBA start, letting Green play his usual power forward role. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Brandin Podziemski 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Personalize your Rotoworld feed by favoriting players 
 Brandin Podziemski recorded 18 points (7-of-14 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), seven rebounds, five assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Nuggets. 
 Back in the lineup after sitting out Saturday’s loss to the Suns, Podziemski recorded his second 18-point game of the season. He played 33 minutes against the Nuggets, a positive sign given the back issue that kept Podz out of the Warriors’ October 21 season opener. Golden State has three more games in Week 2, ending with a Sunday/Monday back-to-back, so another injury management night could be on the horizon for Podziemski. 
 Stephen Curry 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #30 
 Stephen Curry (knee) and Brandin Podziemski (back) are available for Monday’s game against the Nuggets. 
 Curry and Podziemski did not play in Saturday’s loss to the Suns for injury management reasons. Their returns will push Brandon Williams and Will Richard to the bench. 
 De'Anthony Melton 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #8 
 De’Anthony Melton finished Saturday’s loss to the Suns with 25 points (8-of-13 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, three steals and four three-pointers. 
 Melton didn’t start Saturday’s game, but Stephen Curry’s and Brandin Podziemski’s absences gave him more opportunities. Melton took advantage, scoring 25 points, the most he’s scored in a game since 27 against the Wizards on March 16. Add in the rebounds, assists and steals, and Saturday night was a good one for fantasy managers who slotted Melton into their lineups. 
 Stephen Curry 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #30 
 Stephen Curry (knee) is out for Saturday’s game against the Suns. 
 No surprise here as Curry said after Friday’s loss to the Grizzlies that he probably wouldn’t play against the Suns Saturday. With Brandin Podziemski also out, De’Anthony Melton and Will Richard could start and see significant minutes. 
 Brandin Podziemski 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Brandin Podziemski (head) accounted for 18 points (7-of-17 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, three assists, three steals, one block and two three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Grizzlies. 
 Podziemski entered Friday’s game dealing with a sore lower back that kept him out of Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers. It didn’t help matters that he took an inadvertent forearm from Grizzlies center Zach Edey to the head early in the first quarter. Podziemski returned later in the period after a trip to the locker room and logged 33 minutes overall. He finished with a complete stat line, but this is it for Podz in Week 1. After Friday’s defeat, he said he would not play in Saturday’s game against the Suns.

 Podziemski is available after sitting out Wednesday’s season-opening loss to the Lakers. His return likely pushes De’Anthony Melton to the bench. 
 Brandin Podziemski 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Brandin Podziemski (back) is probable for Friday’s game against the Grizzlies. 
 Podziemski is trending in the right direction after he was initially listed as questionable with a back ailment. He missed Wednesday’s loss against the Lakers with the same injury. Now that he’s been upgraded to probable, Podziemski, who appeared in all 82 games last season, should start alongside Stephen Curry against the Grizzlies Friday.

 Brandin Podziemski (back) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Grizzlies. 
 Podziemski did not play in Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers, leading to De’Anthony Melton taking the starting spot. Melton played 21 minutes, while reserves Will Richard and Brandon Williams played 20 and 18 minutes, respectively. Expect a similar rotation if Podziemski can’t play on Friday. 
 Brandin Podziemski

 Guard 
 #2 
 Warriors head coach Steve Kerr said on Wednesday that he’s hopeful Brandin Podziemski (back) will return for Friday’s game against the Grizzlies. 
 After missing practice on Monday, Podziemski will miss Wednesday’s opener against the Lakers due to lower back soreness. However, he may not be out long, with Kerr hoping Podz can play on Friday. De’Anthony Melton is the player whose role may expand the most while Podziemski sits.

 Brandin Podziemski (back) has been ruled out against the Lakers on Wednesday. 
 Podz missed practice on Monday and will now be unavailable for the season opener. There are high expectations for the type of impact he’ll make this season, so they’ll certainly miss him. De’Anthony Melton will likely replace him in the starting unit.

 Jalen Johnson had 12 points (4-of-12 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), nine rebounds, 11 assists, two blocks and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s game against the Heat. 
 Johnson was just one rebound shy of a triple-double. While that makes for a somewhat solid stat line, he also shot 4-of-12 from the field and was -23 in 36 minutes in a 12-points loss at home to the Heat, who entered play Wednesday winless. It’ll be a quick turnaround for Johnson as the Hawks take on the Cavaliers at home Thursday. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 RJ Barrett with a monster 25 points (9-of-8 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), nine rebounds, six assists, a steal and three 3-pointers on Wednesday against the Magic. 
 RJ Barrett took the shots early in this game in the first game without Kawhi and was efficient from the field. Notably, he was on the exercise bike at multiple points in this game, so it could be something to monitor. If you got RJ Barrett in fantasy, you should be really happy about what he’s been doing. He won’t get you many defensive numbers but he will certainly score, and get you some rebounds. There’s an opportunity with Kawhi out, so there could be room to sell-high if someone gives you a good offer.

 Scottie Barnes has 28 points (11-of-17 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, four assists, three steals, and two blocks in 129-99 win against the Magic. 
 With no Kawhi Leonard, Scottie Barnes made up the difference and kept the defense aggressive in this game. He’s very good as a roamer and can get a lot of his defensive numbers that way. If you drafted Scottie Barnes, you should be feeling very happy about that decision and should be in contention to finish in the top 10 of fantasy rankings this season.

 Nickeil Alexander-Walker had 23 points (8-of-18 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, one assist, one steal and five three-pointers against the Heat on Wednesday. 
 Alexander-Walker led the Hawks with 23 points, breaking a stretch of three consecutive games where he fell short of at least 20 points. He’s made at least four three-pointers in three of five games so far this season. Alexander-Walker averaged a career-high 3.2 made three-pointers per game last season and he’s carried his outside shooting success into this year.

 Jase Richardson got 10 points (4-of-8 FGs), a rebound, an assist, and two 3-pointers in start against Raptors. 
 Even though he started, Jase didn’t end up playing starters minutes. After playing the first four minutes, he didn’t return to the game until the third quarter since the Magic needed more size to match against Toronto. In college he was known as a connective glue guy while being efficient, and that’s exactly what he’s done up to this point. In dynasty, the ceiling will depend on how much of a scorer and shooter he can be, because it’s getting harder to play at his size if he’s not a PG, which he really isn’t.

 Desmond Bane put up 13 points (3-of-14 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), five rebounds, four assists, a steal, two blocks, and two 3-pointers in 99-129 loss to Raptors. 
 It was a bad night for Bane as he couldn’t get shots to fall against the Raptors. Bane in the past two seasons has shot 48.4% from the field, but he hasn’t shot very well this season. There is a good track record to indicate that there will be a bounce back from Bane and to not panic too much about his efficiency. He at least got you five rebounds and four assists to give you some value.

 Tristan Da Silva with 20 points (8-of-10 FGs, 0-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, an assist, and four 3-pointers in 30 minutes off the bench against Raptors. 
 Anthony Black didn’t have it tonight, so Da Silva got some more extended run and did not disappoint. He’s not someone that is inherently a scorer, but he was hitting shots tonight when not many other people on the Magic were scoring against the Raptors. He’s a points and 3-point streamer if you’re looking for it in but he won’t shoot as efficiently as he did most nights.

 Franz Wagner had 15 points (4-of-11 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, and seven turnovers in blowout loss to Raptors.
 Franz was one of the only players that could get shots up in this game. The Magic struggled with efficiency as they dealt with the Raptors aggressive defense, but you can see it affected Franz with the 7 turnovers. The Magic will play the Raptors again on Friday and will get a second chance at redemption where he will look to have a better performance.

 Pelle Larsson had 17 points (6-of-12 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, eight assists, one steal and two three-pointers against the Hawks on Wednesday. 
 Larsson has recorded at least 12 points, at least four assists, at least one steal and at least one three-pointer in three consecutive games. He’s also played at least 31 minutes in three consecutive games and had at least six rebounds in two of the last three games. Larsson is turning out to be a key bench player for Heat and worth considering picking up given his recent production.

 Kelly Oubre with 15 points (5-of-10 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, an assist, and a three taking over Haliburton in the starting lineup. 
 With no Haliburton and Zubac tonight, Oubre’s scoring was much needed in the Pacers come back. From a fantasy perspective, he doesn’t provide much outside of decent scoring and occasional rebounding, so he’s fine if you need a boost in those categories, but he will have other games where the shot isn’t there and there’s not a lot there from a fantasy perspective.
